evidence: 128 tracked investments including three RWA-categorised deals: Brickken (15 January 2025), Pointsville (4 September 2025) and Shift (12 September 2025). No insurance or reinsurance holding appears.
notes: Three RWA deals inside nine months in 2025 suggests an active and current RWA thesis — the most RWA-directional of the pure crypto funds in this batch.

name: SoftBank Vision Fund
thesis: ZhongAn (2018), PolicyBazaar, Ping An Good Doctor. A real insurtech record at cheque sizes far above a seed.
evidence: The Vision Fund's investments include Chinese online-only insurer ZhongAn — an investment reported on 21 August 2018 ('China's Online Insurer ZhongAn to Get Investment from SoftBank for Overseas Growth') — as well as Indian insurance marketplace PolicyBazaar and Ping An Good Doctor.
notes: Genuine insurtech track record, but cheque sizes are far above an $8.5M seed — realistic only as a later-stage follow-on, not a seed lead. Fund created May 2017.

name: Solana Ventures (Solana Foundation)
evidence: Tracked rounds through 2024-2025 — including Exponent (30 Apr 2025), Squads (29 Apr 2025), Hylo (7 Aug 2025), ZAR (30 Apr 2025), Streamflow (28 Oct 2024) and Infinex (25 Sep 2024) — contain no insurance, reinsurance or RWA-categorised company.
notes: Ecosystem context, not an investment: SurancePlus announced tokenised reinsurance RWA securities issued on Solana through HCI Group's Fortex Re programme (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/crypto/articles/suranceplus-launch-tokenized-reinsurance-rwa-202100683.html). Solana is already a venue for on-chain reinsurance even though its venture arm has not funded the category.

name: Sompo Holdings
thesis: Japanese P&C group that bought Canopius (2014) and Endurance (2016). Group M&A, not venture cheques; Sompo Digital Lab's mandate could not be verified. A strategic capacity conversation, and a Plug and Play founding partner.
evidence: Sompo Holdings, the Japanese P&C and life insurance group, acquired Lloyd's insurer Canopius Group for £594M in April 2014 and completed its $6.3bn acquisition of Bermuda-based insurer/reinsurer Endurance Specialty in October 2016. Earlier deals include Taisei Fire & Marine (Dec 2002) and Nipponkoa Insurance (Sept 2014).
notes: Evidence is group M&A, not venture cheques. sompo-hd.com did not surface Sompo Digital Lab or any named startup investment, so the venture arm's activity is unverified here — confirm the Digital Lab's mandate before approaching.

name: Sora Ventures
evidence: 30 tracked investments concentrated on the Bitcoin / Ordinals ecosystem — Saturn (15 Jan 2025), Ordzaar (21 Oct 2024), Satflow (14 Aug 2024), OrdinalsBot (26 Mar 2024), Liquidium (11 Dec 2023). No insurance, reinsurance or RWA-categorised company appears.
notes: Bitcoin-native thesis (Ordinals, BRC-20, Bitcoin DeFi) — poor fit for insurance risk transfer.

name: SOSV
evidence: Deep-tech accelerator-VC running HAX (hard tech, Newark NJ, opened April 2024) and IndieBio (life sciences, NY office opened January 2023). Named holdings are Opentrons, Formlabs, NotCo, Prolific Machines, unSpun, Neptune Robotics, Smartex and BitMEX; around 150 climate-tech startups as of November 2021. No insurance, risk-transfer or RWA holding found.
notes: Climate exposure is on the mitigation/hardware side, not climate risk transfer. BitMEX is its only notable crypto name.

name: Spark Capital
evidence: Named investments include Twitter (Series B, June 2008), Deel (Series B, 2020) and Anthropic (Series C, 2022), plus Coinbase, Affirm, Plaid, Ramp, Cruise and Discord. No insurance, insurtech, reinsurance or tokenised-RWA company appears.
notes: Strong fintech and crypto exposure (Coinbase, Affirm, Plaid) but nothing in risk transfer. Coinbase is arguably regulated market infrastructure, but no date for that investment was available so it does not meet the 'adjacent' bar.

name: Speedinvest
thesis: European early-stage fund with Wefox and Luko (acquired by Allianz, Jan 2024). Distribution insurtech; entry dates not confirmed.
evidence: Speedinvest's Dealroom investor profile lists insurtechs Wefox and Luko among its 339 portfolio companies, within a 100-company fintech book that also includes Tide, Wayflyer, Bitpanda and Moove. Luko was acquired by Allianz on 26 January 2024.
notes: speedinvest.com returns 403 to automated fetches, so no Speedinvest deal date could be confirmed — hence year 0; the 2024 Luko date is the Allianz acquisition, not Speedinvest's entry. European early-stage (pre-seed to growth), portfolio HQs concentrated in the UK (87), Germany (82) and Austria (51).

name: Steakhouse Financial
thesis: Not a fund — an on-chain credit advisory and vault curator. A structuring or distribution partner, not seed capital.
evidence: Describes itself as 'the credit stack for the stablecoin economy', curating on-chain credit vaults on Morpho and Kamino and running Grove, 'an institutional-grade credit and liquidity protocol built on DeFi rails'. Its site displays Coinbase, BlackRock, Societe Generale, Robinhood, MetaMask, Compound and Morpho as partners (page dated to 1 September 2026).
notes: An advisory firm, underwriter and vault curator — not a venture fund. Likely a distribution, structuring or underwriting partner rather than a source of seed capital. No insurance work mentioned on the site.

name: Stratos
evidence: No reliable page for an investment firm named Stratos could be loaded: cryptorank.io fund pages for 'stratos' and 'stratos-ventures', RootData, DropsTab and ICO Drops profiles, and the domains stratos.xyz and stratos.vc all returned 404 or empty content.
notes: The name is ambiguous — a Stratos decentralised-storage project, Stratos Technologies (a US private-credit firm) and others share it. Needs the firm's website from the original source list to disambiguate before any outreach.

name: Sumitomo Life Innovation
thesis: Sumitomo Life is an LP in Anthemis's insurance fund (Feb 2020) and put $90M into Singapore Life (2019); runs the Sumisei Innovation Fund with SBI. If the Sumitomo Insurance MoU sits with Sumitomo Life, this is its venture door — reachable through Anthemis either way.
evidence: Sumitomo Life invested US$90m in Singapore-based insurtech Singapore Life for a ~25% stake in July 2019. It is also a named investor in the Anthemis Insurance Venture Growth Fund I, closed February 2020.
notes: Anthemis fund LP position corroborated at https://www.carriermanagement.com/news/2020/02/27/203762.htm. Sumitomo Life also runs the Y8bn Sumisei Innovation Fund with SBI Investment, targeting insurtech and healthtech. Distinct from Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance Venture Capital (MS&AD group).

name: Summit Partners
thesis: Acturis (exited 2019), Insurcomm, Beyond Risk (captive management), DocuSketch. Growth equity, $44bn AUM.
evidence: Summit Partners made a growth equity investment in Acturis, a SaaS platform for the general insurance industry, and exited when Astorg agreed to acquire a minority shareholding in March 2019. Its insurance-services portfolio also includes Insurcomm, Beyond Risk (alternative risk / captive management) and DocuSketch (claims scoping).
notes: Growth equity, not seed - $44B+ AUM, typical cheque far above an $8.5M seed. Insurance exposure is software and services, not risk transfer or ILS.

name: Swiss Re
thesis: Top-tier ILS and cat-bond counterparty; iptiQ led Getsafe's Series B (2020) and Swiss Re joined the 2021 extension. On the original target list as a carrier. A strategic and capacity relationship, not a seed cheque — its former CEO questioned reinsurers acting as VCs.
evidence: Swiss Re's iptiQ led digital insurer Getsafe's $30m Series B in December 2020, and Swiss Re joined the extended $93m Series B reported in October 2021. Swiss Re states its innovation strategy covers data and analytics, AI, parametrics, blockchain and smart contracts.
notes: Extended round at https://www.reinsurancene.ws/swiss-re-joins-insurtech-getsafes-93m-series-b/. Swiss Re is itself a top-tier ILS/cat bond counterparty, so it is a strategic as much as a financial investor; its former CEO publicly questioned reinsurers acting as VC funds.

name: Symbolic Capital
evidence: No evidence found of insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investing. Portfolio is web3 gaming and infrastructure - Polyhedra Network, IndiGG, Arcana, Syndicate, YGG SEA.
notes: Founded 2021, formerly Hyperedge Capital. 40+ portfolio companies, all web3/AI/DeFi/NFT; nothing insurance- or RWA-adjacent surfaced in two searches.

name: Synaitken
evidence: No evidence found of insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investing. Aggregator profiles describe a Switzerland-based blockchain, security and privacy investor with a single recorded investment, activity peaking in 2020.
notes: Very thin footprint - one recorded ~$1m investment and no official website surfaced. May be dormant; treat as low priority.

name: Systemic Ventures
thesis: New (2025) fund that joined Tether's $8M KAIO round (Apr 2026) — tokenised-fund rails, the closest adjacency to programmable risk transfer.
evidence: Systemic Ventures joined Tether's $8m round in KAIO, announced 20 April 2026. KAIO is regulated in ADGM, Cayman and Singapore and builds infrastructure for institutional managers to issue, redeem and transfer tokenised fund shares, having tokenised funds from Hamilton Lane, BlackRock, Laser Digital and Brevan Howard.
notes: New firm (founded 2025), ~9 investments across AI, Web3, DePIN. Tokenised-fund rails are the closest fit to programmable risk transfer; no insurance exposure. Do not confuse with systemic.ventures, an unrelated tech due-diligence firm.

name: Tezos Foundation
thesis: Joined Fraktion's RWA tokenisation seed (Feb 2025); ecosystem funder whose capital is tied to building on Tezos.
evidence: The Tezos Foundation participated in the EUR1.1m seed round of Fraktion, an end-to-end real-world-asset tokenisation platform for real estate, announced early February 2025. It is also collaborating with Xalts on institutional RWA tokenisation.
notes: Ecosystem funder rather than a conventional VC - capital is tied to building on Tezos, which may not suit a chain-agnostic risk-infrastructure startup. No insurance or risk-transfer investment found.

name: Tiger Global
thesis: Led Plum (India employee health, 2021); Zopper. Distribution, India, growth.
evidence: Tiger Global led the $15.6m round in Indian employee-health-insurance startup Plum in May 2021. Tiger-backed insurance distribution platform Zopper raised a $75m Series C in September 2022.
notes: Insurtech exposure is distribution and employee benefits, mostly India, not risk transfer or ILS. Zopper reference: https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/story/tiger-global-backed-insurance-tech-start-up-zopper-raises-75-mn-in-series-c-funding-347658-2022-09-20 - Tiger was an existing backer, the 2022 round was led by Creaegis.

name: TKX Capital
evidence: No evidence found of insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investing. TKX closed a US$25m crypto venture fund focused on Web3, NFT, metaverse, GameFi, DeFi and blockchain infrastructure; named holdings include Mask, Polygon, Bloktopia, Serum, Alien Worlds and Bit2Me.
notes: Founded March 2021 by former OKX/Huobi executives; positions itself as a crypto investment bank. Nothing insurance- or RWA-related surfaced.

name: Tokio Marine Future Fund
thesis: Tokio Marine's $42M venture fund writes $500k–$3M into seed and Series A insurtech and climate-risk companies (Anzen, Nov 2025; Pano AI), and the parent can act as capacity. No parametric deal found yet — stage and mandate carry it.
evidence: Tokio Marine launched the $42m Tokio Marine Future Fund in April 2022 to back seed and Series A companies in insurtech, fintech and climate risk. Its most recent recorded investment was on 13 November 2025 in Anzen, an insurance company; it also joined Pano AI's Series B (wildfire detection) alongside Liberty Mutual Strategic Ventures.
notes: Strong fit on paper: $500k-$3m cheques into seed/Series A, explicitly insurtech and climate risk, and Tokio Marine can act as a capacity provider. Fund managed with World Innovation Lab (WiL). Fund launch: https://techcrunch.com/2022/04/19/japanese-insurance-company-tokio-marine-launches-cvc-fund-to-back-early-stage-startups/

name: Tomahawk VC
evidence: No named insurance, risk-transfer or RWA portfolio company could be confirmed. Tomahawk.VC is a Swiss pre-seed/seed fintech and DeFi investor active since 2019 with 36 investments; the named holdings that surfaced are DFINITY, MENU and Locatee.
notes: Worth a second look despite the verdict: aggregator profiles state the portfolio spans blockchain and insurance and that the firm works on insurance products, but two searches surfaced no named insurtech holding or date. Cheque size USD 250k-1.5m, fintech/DeFi thesis - thematically close.

name: TomoChain
evidence: No evidence found of insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investing. TomoChain's investing arm LuaVentures launched in August 2021 with a ~$2m fund and made 6 investments in DeFi, NFT and infrastructure; its latest recorded deal was IQ Protocol's Series A on 3 March 2022.
notes: The chain has since rebranded as Viction, and the investing arm (LuaVentures) appears inactive after early 2022. Likely a dead entry for outreach purposes.

name: TRG Capital
evidence: No dated insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investment could be confirmed. TRG Capital is an Amsterdam blockchain investor founded in 2017 with a reported 61 portfolio companies including Razor Network, Polywrap, AVA, Boba, KRNL Labs and Rome Blockchain.
notes: Portfolio reportedly includes Credit Coop, an on-chain credit protocol, which would be adjacent - but no date or primary source was found, so it is not scored. Name collides with TRG Capital Management (trgcap.com), an unrelated US investment manager.

name: TTV Capital
thesis: Insurtech is a core vertical; pre-seed to Series A, $2–7M first cheques (Stream Claims seed, Oct 2024). Claims and workflow, not risk transfer.
evidence: TTV Capital participated in the $5.3m seed round of Stream Claims, an AI medical-document-review insurtech for workers' compensation, announced 11 October 2024 and led by Spark Capital. Insurtech is one of TTV's stated core verticals.
notes: Good stage fit: pre-seed to Series A, $2m-$7m initial cheques, Fund VI closed March 2023, ~$250m AUM. Thesis also covers Web3 and crypto alongside insurtech.

name: Tungsten Custody
evidence: Tungsten Custody Solutions is not an investor. It is a digital-asset custodian founded in 2023, regulated by the FSRA in Abu Dhabi Global Market, and it was acquired by Zodia Custody, which now operates it as its ADGM-licensed entity.
notes: A custodian (ADGM), acquired by Zodia; not an investor.

name: UDHC Finance
thesis: Holds OnRe, the on-chain reinsurance protocol, on its own portfolio page next to Maple, Circle and Canton — the only fund here with on-chain reinsurance beside on-chain credit and tokenisation rails. Run by former Maker Foundation operators; small cheques.
evidence: UDHC's own portfolio page lists OnRe, the on-chain reinsurance protocol, under asset origination. OnRe raised a $1.9m seed in March 2026 and a $5m Series A in May 2026 co-led by Forward Industries and RockawayX. UDHC also holds Maple Finance, Membrane, Circle, Canton Network and Oasis Pro.
notes: Best-matched investor in this batch: the only one holding an on-chain reinsurance company alongside on-chain credit and tokenisation infrastructure. Dates given are OnRe's round dates - UDHC's own entry date is not published on its portfolio page. Run by former Maker Foundation operators; thesis is explicitly TradFi/DeFi convergence.

name: Uncork Capital
evidence: No evidence found of insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investing. Two searches surfaced only consumer, SaaS and marketplace holdings - Postmates, Eventbrite, Calm, Intercom, LaunchDarkly, Carrot Fertility, Shippo, Loft Orbital.
notes: Seed specialist ($1.5m-$3m for 12-15%), closed $300m across two funds in May 2025, so stage and cheque size fit an $8.5M seed. The firm keeps an 'Insurance' tag on its Medium blog (medium.com/uncorkcapital/tagged/insurance) but no named insurtech holding was confirmed.

name: Underscore VC
thesis: Three consecutive Hi Marley rounds (2019–2021) and Herald (quote-and-bind APIs) — real conviction in insurance infrastructure, on the carrier-workflow side.
evidence: Underscore VC backed Hi Marley, a conversational platform for P&C insurance, through its $8.7m Series A (June 2019), co-led its $8m Series A1 (June 2020) and joined its $25m Series B (March 2021). Its portfolio also includes Herald, which provides quote-and-bind API infrastructure for commercial insurance.
notes: Repeat insurance-infrastructure investor with real conviction (three consecutive Hi Marley rounds). Exposure is carrier workflow and distribution APIs, not risk transfer, ILS or on-chain.

name: Union Square Ventures
thesis: Agentero (seed 2017) and CoverWallet (Series A 2016) beside deep crypto conviction (Polygon, Stacks). A rare combination; the insurance deals are nine years old.
evidence: USV's portfolio page lists Agentero, an insurtech for independent agents, at seed in 2017, and CoverWallet, small-business commercial insurance, at Series A in 2016 (since acquired by Aon). It also holds crypto and on-chain companies including Stacks, Polygon, WalletConnect and Daylight.
notes: Rare combination of insurance and deep crypto conviction in one portfolio, but the insurance deals are ~9 years old and there is no parametric, cat-risk or ILS exposure. Most recent on-chain deals: Daylight (seed 2024), Recall (Series A 2025), Pascal (Series A 2026).

name: VanEck Ventures
thesis: $30M pre-seed and seed fund (Oct 2024) whose core themes are tokenisation and stablecoin platforms; backed Manifest (Mar 2025). Asset-manager parent with tokenised-product distribution; no insurance deal.
evidence: VanEck launched VanEck Ventures in October 2024, a $30m pre-seed and seed fund whose core themes are tokenisation, stablecoin platforms and internet-native financial marketplaces. It backed Manifest, a platform bringing US real estate into DeFi via a tokenised real-estate product, in March 2025.
notes: Manifest report: mitrade.com live news, 21 March 2025. Asset-manager parent with deep tokenised-product distribution; no insurance or risk-transfer investment found. Fund launch also covered by CoinDesk (9 October 2024) and The Block.

name: Venture Collective
evidence: No evidence found of insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investing. The Venture Collective is an early-stage impact investor whose named holdings are X-Energy, Life Biosciences, Universal Quantum, Axiom Space, Unnatural Products, Wonderbelly, Orbem and Qloo.
notes: Thesis is life sciences, planetary sustainability and digital infrastructure. Climate adjacency exists at the thesis level but there is no risk-transfer, insurance or financial-infrastructure holding.

name: ViaBTC Capital
evidence: No evidence found of insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investing. ViaBTC Capital is the CVC arm of the ViaBTC/CoinEx exchange group in Shenzhen; named deals include BEVM ($10m), Kelp DAO ($9m private sale), WOO Network ($30m Series A) and Earn Network ($2.7m seed).
notes: Roughly 18-25 recorded investments, all Web3/Layer-2/DeFi infrastructure. Ranked 'Tier 4' by ICO Drops. No insurance or tokenised-RWA exposure.

name: Visary Capital
thesis: Tokenised RWA or regulated financial infrastructure only — no insurance or risk-transfer deal found.
evidence: Visary Capital's named holdings include Kraken, the regulated cryptocurrency exchange, which raised $800m at a $20bn valuation in November 2025, plus Hut 8 (December 2025), Turing (March 2025) and OneBrief (January 2026).
notes: Scored adjacent only because a regulated exchange counts as financial market infrastructure - there is no tokenised-RWA, on-chain credit or insurance holding. Thesis is the 'Digital Autonomous Crypto Compute Economy', i.e. crypto plus AI compute. Weak fit for risk transfer.

name: w3 fund
evidence: No named portfolio company could be confirmed. w3.fund is a Berlin investment house running w3.ventures (pre-seed/seed Web3) and w3.wave (liquid token fund); it states its target areas as stablecoins, tokenisation, Web3 x AI, B2B use cases, DeFi and gaming, but publishes no holdings.
notes: Thesis overlap on tokenisation and stablecoins is real, so worth a conversation despite the 'none' - the verdict reflects an absence of published, dated deals rather than a confirmed absence of interest. No insurance exposure found.

name: Xterio
evidence: No evidence found of insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investing. Xterio is a Web3 gaming infrastructure and publishing company - wallet, publishing, developer kit and account-abstracted identity - not an investment firm; it lists no portfolio companies.
notes: A Web3 game publisher that is itself venture-backed; not an investor.

name: Zilliqa Capital
evidence: No insurance, risk-transfer or RWA investment could be confirmed. The firm's own site states it was founded as Zilliqa Capital Pte. Ltd. in 2021 and converted to Rule72 Pte. Ltd. in 2022; it is a Singapore permanent capital vehicle investing in AI, advanced fintech and Web3 across APAC, and publishes no portfolio holdings.
notes: Renamed Rule72 in 2022.

name: Sumitomo Mitsui (SMBC) venture activity in insurtech or digital assets
evidence: No insurtech or digital-asset investment was found. SMBC Venture Capital, the Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group arm, describes itself as industry- and stage-agnostic with 400+ IPO'd portfolio companies; the named holdings on its site are Everee, Basic, Schoo, AstroScale, Heartseed, QPS Research Institute and Chordia Therapeutics.
notes: Named holdings skew biotech, space and education. NAME CONFUSION WARNING: 'Sumitomo Mitsui' (SMBC/SMFG, banking) is a different group from 'Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance' (MS&AD), whose CVC arm MSIVC is an active insurance investor - see https://tracxn.com/d/venture-capital/mitsui-sumitomo-insurance-venture-capital/__iycospEydacQMAj_FWpHxU1a0p_TvJQlyhQp9XpQhuU. MSIVC is the entity worth adding to the list.

name: Mitsui & Co venture arm in insurtech or digital assets
evidence: No insurtech or digital-asset venture investment by Mitsui & Co (the trading house) was found in two searches; no active venture-arm portfolio page could be located.

If the intent behind this list entry was Japanese insurance CVC, MSIVC is the right target; if it was genuinely Mitsui & Co, nothing relevant was found.

evidence: No evidence found of insurance, insurtech, blockchain or digital-asset investing. Marubeni Ventures, established June 2019 in Tokyo, lists Floadia, D-ID, GrubMarket, NOIN, Orbit Fab, NeuroBlade, Revelio Labs, Bumper, Linkwith, River and L Pixel.
